questions.prompt: What does Runway say a Recipe is?

options.text: A prebuilt multi-step workflow that wraps several generations behind a single call
options.explanation: Right. You do not have to orchestrate the steps yourself.

options.text: A single generation with a longer prompt
options.explanation: A recipe wraps several generations, not one.

options.text: A saved prompt that you reuse by hand
options.explanation: The primer calls recipes prebuilt workflows. They run several generations in one call.

questions.prompt: Why pin a recipe to a dated version on client work?

options.text: Only dated versions can be waited on
options.explanation: Both kinds return a task. They follow the same contract.

options.text: The behavior stays the same, instead of following the newest stable version
options.explanation: Right. Runway says a dated version pins behavior and unsafe-latest tracks the newest.

options.text: A dated version is always free
options.explanation: Nothing in the docs ties a dated version to price.

questions.prompt: When you define the tools for a chain yourself, who runs each step?

options.text: Your application runs each tool call and sends the result back to the model.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says your application can continue the flow for as many tool calls as the task requires. Anthropic says your code executes client tools and returns a tool_result.

options.text: The model runs each step itself.
options.explanation: Google says the model does not execute the function itself. The vendors describe a call and a result.

options.text: The vendor's server always runs every step.
options.explanation: That holds only for server or built-in tools. For tools you define, your application runs the call.
